# The production Compose file is generated by the AppHost and committed

Production runs from `deploy/docker-compose.yaml`, which `aspire publish` writes from `src/AppHost/Production.cs`, and
which is committed rather than written by hand or generated at deploy time. The AppHost already describes every service,
so generating the file keeps one description of them; committing it means a deployment needs only that file and
`.env.example`, not the repo or the Aspire CLI. `ProductionComposeTests` fails while the committed file differs from a
fresh publish, so the two can't drift apart.

## Consequences

- Change the deployment in `Production.cs` and run `src/AppHost/publish-deployment.sh`; an edit to the Compose file
  itself is overwritten.
- Anything Aspire's Compose model can't express can't be in the file, such as `pids_limit`, unless the generated YAML is
  post-processed, which the drift test would then have to do too.
- Development and production are separate graphs in the AppHost (`Development.cs`, `Production.cs`), since production
  runs every service in a container on networks of its own, which development can't without losing the Backend's
  debugger.
